newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS - Roche profit gain disappoints market.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Roche profit gain disappoints market.

text.p: Swiss pharmaceuticals group Roche Holding AG on Tuesday reported a 16 percent rise in first-half net profit but analysts and markets were slightly disappointed with the operating performance.
"The results look fine but I would have liked a little more," said Peter McDougall of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell .
Roche said it expected sales to continue on a positive track in the second half of 1996 and confirmed that it still expects full-year profit to exceed 1995's 3.37 billion francs ($2.8 billion).

"Barring extraordinary events, we can again expect to see a good overall result for the 1996 business year and in particular another increase in consolidated net profit," Roche said in its interim report.
The increase in first-half net profit to 2.21 billion francs was roughly in line with forecasts of a 17 percent rise.
However, analysts had looked for Roche's operating profit to rise 10 percent or more. But it grew by 7.6 percent to 1.95 billion francs on sales of 7.77 billion, up 8.0 percent.
"The operating result could have been better," said Christian Prinz of Credit Suisse's CS Research.

Some analysts, such as Beat Alpiger of Bank Julius Baer, said they would probably revise downward their forecast for the entire year but any adjustment would take place later following a teleconference with Roche officials.
In contrast to Roche's slightly disappointing operating result, its financial result rose 31 percent to 786 million francs, helping to compensate.
The stock market shared analysts' slight disappointment, marking down Roche's non-voting equity certificates.
During the afternoon Roche's certificates were trading 25 francs lower at 9,405 francs in a generally higher Swiss market.

Roche said the positive development in lowering manufacturing costs in the first half had been offset by several factors, including a reduction in reference prices in Japan, lower prices in Italy and price erosion for fragrances.
In addition, it suffered from price cuts in the laboratory business in the United States and increased marketing costs in the pharmaceuticals division.
Alpiger said it was difficult to pinpoint exactly why Roche's operating results were below expectations and he was looking to Roche for further clarification of financial results.
"The bulk of profits come in the first half so Roche would have to raise results substantially in the second half to live up to expectations," Alpiger said.
Analysts expect Roche to report a full-year net profit of around four billion francs, up around 19 percent from 1995's 3.37 billion.
While the strong financial result reflects the positive state of financial markets in the first half, analysts said they still looked to Roche to turn some of its cash pile into operating assets.
"I am sure Roche is on the acquisition trail because the company is feeling the pinch," McDougall said, referring to the performance of its operating results.
At the end of 1995 Roche had marketable securities of 11.9 billion francs and cash of 2.6 billion.
($1=1.1893 Swiss Franc)
